vendors.strategy: The foundational philosophy of eMemory's patent portfolio is 'Zero Mask Adder' and '100% Standard CMOS Logic Process Compatibility'. Unlike conventional eFlash architectures that demand 3 to 8 additional specialized polysilicon masks or high-temperature thermal steps, eMemory's patent topology builds entirely upon native gate dielectrics, polysilicon gates, and well diffusion regions available in standard CMOS logic. Its patent map unfolds across two foundational vectors: the charge-storage trajectory (NeoBit floating-gate OTP → NeoEE capacitive-coupling MTP → NeoMTP erase-gate MTP) and the dielectric-physics trajectory (NeoFuse gate-oxide antifuse OTP → NeoPUF quantum-tunneling hardware security root of trust), spanning legacy sub-micron nodes down to 2nm GAA nanosheet architectures.

patents.title: Method of programming a series PMOS embedded EPROM cell
patents.coreProblem: Conventional EPROM/OTP cells require dedicated control gates and additional polysilicon layers for capacitive coupling, escalating logic process wafer costs. How can efficient electron injection be achieved on standard PMOS devices lacking a control gate?
patents.mechanism: Specifies a pair of series-connected p-channel MOS transistors: a first PMOS serving as a select transistor, and a second PMOS having an isolated floating gate. Applying positive 3–8V bias between Source Line (SL) and N-Well while biasing the drain negatively induces drain band-to-band tunneling holes. Secondary hot electrons generated by impact ionization are accelerated by vertical oxide fields across the 3.15 eV barrier into the floating gate.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 specifies a series PMOS structure devoid of a control gate, biasing the source and N-well to a common positive potential while applying negative drain bias to inject secondary avalanche electrons into the floating gate.
patents.productLink: The founding patent behind NeoBit mass production, widely deployed in PMICs, audio DAC calibration, and LCD driver ICs.

patents.title: Programmed logic non-volatile memory cell with retained charges
patents.coreProblem: Written floating-gate cells must ensure robust charge retention under extreme high-temperature environments while providing high signal-to-noise margins for sense amplifiers.
patents.mechanism: Programmed floating gates retain a stable negative charge packet. In PMOS physics, negative gate charge shifts the threshold voltage negatively, driving the storage PMOS into a conductive state under read bias, while unprogrammed cells remain cut off. Arrhenius extrapolations demonstrate data retention exceeding 10 years at 125°C.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 defines an unprogrammed cell in a non-conductive state and a programmed cell retaining negative charges on the floating gate to establish a low-resistance conduction path, using channel current level to represent logical data.
patents.productLink: The core reference patent for NeoBit data retention specifications and qualification standards.

patents.title: Antifuse memory cell and operating method thereof
patents.coreProblem: In sub-2nm core gate oxide nodes, traditional antifuses suffer from read disturb and accidental half-select breakdown during array programming.
patents.mechanism: Applies controlled programming pulses across the antifuse gate to trigger localized dielectric soft breakdown. During read, an interrogation voltage below 1.2V senses gate leakage (I_GATE). Unprogrammed gates leak <1pA, while programmed gates conduct several µA, opening an expansive sensing window.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 specifies reading the antifuse below its breakdown threshold voltage and sensing gate leakage current rather than channel conduction to determine programmed states.
patents.productLink: Standard IP across tier-1 foundry PDKs (28nm HPC+, 22ULL, 16FFC, N6/N5).

litigationDefense.title: Patent Tier Defense Strategy & Public Domain Succession
litigationDefense.overview: eMemory represents a quintessential semiconductor IP strategy of "dual-track tiered evolution." Early foundations laid down by NeoBit (US6678190B2 etc.) established 0-mask logic NVM norms. As foundational patents entered the public domain in 2022–2023, eMemory had already secured pervasive patent rings in advanced nodes through NeoFuse (US8514614B2) and NeoPUF (US10204981B2).

keyBattles.heading: Zero-Mask Floating Gate Moat (NeoBit Era)
keyBattles.detail: eMemory secured the premier route for CMOS EPROM via control-gate-free series PMOS with CHEI programming. Competitors seeking 0-mask logic OTP were forced into higher-voltage NMOS breakdown alternatives with inferior yields. Following its 20-year expiration in 2022, this foundational bitcell became free public domain technology, though physically limited to >=65nm.

keyBattles.heading: FinFET & 2nm GAA Advanced Antifuse Ring (NeoFuse Era)
keyBattles.detail: For sub-28nm geometries, eMemory constructed fresh barriers around 3T antifuse topologies (US8982637B2) and gate-tunneling readout techniques (US8514614B2), locking down low-voltage sensing of gate tunneling currents to preempt unauthorized adoption across advanced PDK libraries.

litigationDefense.ftoVerdict: [FTO Guidance] The semiconductor industry may freely practice first-generation NeoBit 2-PMOS CHEI topologies (0.5µm–0.11µm) without royalties. However, sub-28nm antifuse designs employing 3T regulation or sub-breakdown gate tunneling sensing remain actively protected through 2031–2037.

vendors.strategy: The foundational core of Kilopass's patent portfolio pioneered the 'Controlled Gate-Oxide Hard Breakdown' architecture in standard CMOS logic. Moving away from traditional polysilicon eFuses with their high-current explosion, metal splatter, and visible optical microscope traces, Kilopass built an array patent network centered on a 2T/1.5T crosspoint topology. By connecting a select transistor and an antifuse transistor in series, Kilopass eliminated parasitic channel conduction and half-select disturb during high-voltage programming. Extending this to split-well bias isolation, Kilopass established the earliest industry patent standards for embedded logic antifuse OTP.

families.summary: The foundational patent family establishing Kilopass's market standing. By leveraging standard logic thin core oxide to induce irreversible breakdown under 5–7V programming bias, the naturally insulating high-impedance gate transforms into a conductive path of several hundred ohms. The 2T topology ensures unselected cells in large arrays remain free from disturbance, with the breakdown spot buried deep beneath metal interconnect layers, providing natural resistance against optical reverse engineering.

Turning on the access transistor while applying high voltage stress across the antifuse gate creates percolating defect clusters forming a stable conductive filament. Read mode applies standard low operating voltage to sense microampere-level read currents.
patents.claimFocus: Claim 1 claims an array cell and bias control method comprising a standard CMOS access transistor connected in series with an antifuse transistor utilizing controlled gate oxide breakdown as its memory state.
patents.productLink: Kilopass XPM™ (Extra Permanent Memory) flagship product line, widely deployed in DTV decoders and HDMI HDCP root key storage.

litigationDefense.title: Historic Kilopass v. Sidense Litigation & 1T Antifuse Claim Boundaries
litigationDefense.overview: Between 2010 and 2014, Kilopass and Sidense engaged in one of the semiconductor IP sector's landmark patent battles. Kilopass alleged that Sidense 1T-Fuse infringed its foundational XPM patents (US6992925B2 and US6777766B2). The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit (CAFC) ultimately affirmed non-infringement, establishing key boundaries for design-arounds.

keyBattles.heading: Core Disagreement: Scope of "Cross-Point Bitcell"
keyBattles.detail: Kilopass US6992925B2 Claim 1 recited a memory cell formed at the cross-point of WL and BL consisting of a single transistor where gate-to-diffusion overlap experiences dielectric breakdown. Kilopass argued Sidense 1T structure literally matched this limitation.

keyBattles.heading: CAFC Ruling: Substantial Difference of Split-Channel Physics
keyBattles.detail: Sidense successfully established that its patented Split-Channel (US7402855B2) segregates the channel into thick-oxide access and thin-oxide breakdown regions. The thick-oxide segment intrinsically serves as an access switch, distinct from Kilopass cross-point definition under literal and doctrine-of-equivalents standards.

litigationDefense.ftoVerdict: [Major Landmark] Kilopass primary weapon patent US6992925B2 expired in March 2023 after completing its 20-year term. The foundational uniform cross-point 1T gate-oxide breakdown structure is now globally open for royalty-free implementation.

Whereas Kilopass required two transistors in series, Sidense crafted an asymmetric split-channel underneath a single polysilicon gate: one section functioning as a thick-oxide/high-threshold access channel switch, and the adjacent section acting as a thin-oxide breakdown node. This innovation eliminated the separate access transistor, reducing cell area by over 50% compared to 2T cells. Combined with asymmetric lightly doped drain (LDD) masking and differential ultra-low-voltage sensing patents, Sidense eradicated read disturb and filament self-healing, becoming one of the foundry ecosystem's premier 1T OTP architectures.

NSCore pioneer patent US6930349B2 strictly utilizes native CMOS spacers as physical storage nodes, requiring zero DRC modifications or SPICE model changes from silicon foundries.

keyBattles.heading: Gen-2 Pch Schottky Evolution (US8760927B2) & Automotive High-Temp Retention
keyBattles.detail: Overcoming oxide wearout in sub-40nm scaling, NSCore engineered TwinBit Gen-2 with Pch Schottky bitcells using hot-hole write and hot-electron erase. litigationDefense.title: Split-Gate Landmark Patent Moat & Public Domain Opening of ESF1/ESF3
litigationDefense.overview: Founded in 1989 by Dr. Bing Yeh, Silicon Storage Technology (SST) introduced the "Split-Gate Flash Memory Cell," one of the most consequential breakthroughs in semiconductor memory history. Conventional 1T stacked-gate flash suffered chronically from "over-erase," where excessive electron extraction converted cells into depletion-mode switches that permanently shorted bitlines. SST's split-gate structure eliminated this fatal physics flaw, dominating automotive and microcontroller embedded flash for over three decades.

keyBattles.heading: Eliminating the 1T Stacked-Gate Over-Erase Bottleneck (ESF1 US5029130A)
keyBattles.detail: Legacy Intel/AMD/Toshiba stacked-gate architectures required massive on-chip pre-programming state machines before each erase cycle to prevent depletion-mode bitcell leakage. SST patented a split-gate topology where the control gate naturally overlies a dedicated segment of the silicon channel as an integrated access switch. Even if the floating gate is heavily over-erased into negative Vth, the adjacent select channel reliably pinches off, obsoleting complex recovery algorithms.

keyBattles.heading: Gen-3 ESF3 Dedicated Erase Gate (EG) & Source-Side Injection (SSI) Moat (US6747310B2)
keyBattles.detail: Early split-gate devices required high erase voltages applied to control gates. In 2002, SST patented the 1.5T ESF3 topology, introducing a dedicated erase gate (EG) coupled with a sharp polysilicon floating-gate tip. Erase operations utilize intense localized tip field emission, drastically cutting erase voltage; simultaneously, source-side injection (SSI) elevated programming efficiency by 1,000x compared to CHEI, yielding 100K-cycle automotive endurance.

keyBattles.heading: Global Foundry Licensing Consortium & $300M Microchip Acquisition
keyBattles.detail: By licensing SuperFlash across TSMC, UMC, GlobalFoundries, SMIC, and HHGrace, SST achieved ubiquity in embedded flash. In 2010, microcontroller giant Microchip acquired SST for ~$300M, establishing SuperFlash as the core hardware advantage for PIC/AVR MCUs with lifetime shipments surpassing 100 billion dies.

litigationDefense.ftoVerdict: [FTO Guidance] SST pioneer split-gate patent US5029130A expired in August 2009 after completing its full 20-year term. Foundational ESF3 four-gate source-side injection patent US6747310B2 also entered the public domain in April 2022. The semiconductor industry may freely practice asymmetric split-gate and independent erase-gate tip tunneling structures. However, self-aligned 55nm/40nm manufacturing (US8217444B2), 28nm HKMG integration (US8946797B2), and memBrain analog CIM patents (US10658032B2) remain actively enforceable through 2030–2038.

litigationDefense.title: Silicon-Oxide ReRAM BEOL Moat & Conductive Filament Public Domain FTO
litigationDefense.overview: Founded by Israeli and Australian semiconductor veterans, Weebit Nano constructed its IP strategy to overturn the heavy-metal precursor contamination barriers of legacy ReRAM (TaOx, TiO2, HfOx). Traditional foundries dread foreign metals migrating into front-end CMOS gates; Weebit secured exclusive rights to Rice University Professor James Tour's foundational patents, directly utilizing standard CMOS-native porous silicon oxide (SiOx) requiring only 2 low-temperature BEOL masks for 100% zero-contamination foundry qualification across SkyWater and DB HiTek.

keyBattles.heading: Porous Silicon Oxide (SiOx) vs. Exotic Metal Contamination (US10141505B2)
keyBattles.detail: Conventional ReRAM demands unproven noble metals and exotic targets, forcing foundries to establish costly segregated fabrication lines. Weebit's core patent confines switching to porosity-tuned silicon oxide, electro-forming and dissolving reversible silicon nanofilaments using standard foundry PECVD tools, reducing wafer cost by ~70% compared to eFlash.

keyBattles.heading: Neuromorphic Analog Conductance Calibration Moat (US10580980B2)
keyBattles.detail: Analog in-memory computing (CIM) using ReRAM synapses suffers from spontaneous oxygen vacancy relaxation known as conductance drift, corrupting neural network inference accuracy. Weebit patented closed-loop sensing that detects drift with micro-probes before vector-matrix multiplications, applying dynamic restore pulses to preserve inference precision.

keyBattles.heading: Bidirectional Threshold Selector 1S1R Cross-Point Array (US11171286B2)
keyBattles.detail: To bypass the scaling area limit of 1T1R select transistors, Weebit patented highly non-linear bidirectional threshold selectors (>10^5 selectivity), completely suffocating sneak-path leakage in dense cross-point matrices and enabling dense 3D stacking.

litigationDefense.ftoVerdict: [FTO Guidance] Early 2002–2003 foundational metal-oxide resistance switching and electric pulse-induced filament patents (US6815781B2 & US6849891B1) expired in 2022 and 2023, entering the public domain. Industry may freely practice standard 1T1R bipolar switching physics. However, Weebit's proprietary porous SiOx patent (US10141505B2), neuromorphic dynamic conductance calibration (US10580980B2), and 1S1R threshold selector topologies (US11171286B2) remain actively enforceable through 2034, 2037, and 2039.

litigationDefense.title: Quantum Tunneling Geometric Mismatch (NeoPUF) vs. SRAM PUF Zero-BER Moat
litigationDefense.overview: Spun out of eMemory Technology under Chairman Dr. Charles Hsu and CEO Dr. Evans Yang, PUFsecurity revolutionized semiconductor hardware security. Traditional root-of-trust relies on injected keys (susceptible to supply-chain sniffing) or SRAM startup states. However, SRAM PUF suffers from a severe physical defect: temperature fluctuations and aging induce 5%–15% bit error rates (BER), requiring bulky error-correcting codes (ECC helper data) that consume die area and introduce side-channel vulnerabilities. PUFsecurity discarded fragile ECC post-processing, engineering native Zero-BER NeoPUF and PUFrt/PUFcc patent fortress from quantum tunneling physics.

keyBattles.heading: Quantum Geometric Mismatch vs. SRAM Metastable Flipping Risk
keyBattles.detail: SRAM PUF relies on subtle inverter threshold mismatches that flip under extreme temperature (-40°C to 150°C) and supply noise. NeoPUF captures structural variations of atomic defects across paired antifuse dielectric layers; tunneling resistance differences span orders of magnitude, remaining 100% stable under thermal stress and radiation, delivering physical 0% native BER.

keyBattles.heading: Complete Elimination of Helper Data & Side-Channel Attack Surface (US10651268B2)
keyBattles.detail: Because native BER is strictly zero, chips require zero helper data stored in off-chip flash. Attackers cannot reconstruct keys by eavesdropping helper data or analyzing mathematical error distributions, shutting down physical and side-channel vulnerability surfaces.

keyBattles.heading: Quantum Shot Noise TRNG Patent Exclusivity (US10769300B2)
keyBattles.detail: Conventional ring oscillator TRNGs are susceptible to electromagnetic injection locking. PUFsecurity patented entropy harvesting directly from quantum tunneling shot noise, an unmanipulable quantum mechanical phenomenon certified under NIST SP 800-22 and SP 800-90B standards.

keyBattles.heading: Monolithic PUFcc Security Engine & TSMC Advanced Nodes (US11394553B2 / US11880479B2)
keyBattles.detail: Monolithically integrating NeoPUF, secure OTP, quantum TRNG, and post-quantum cryptography (PQC) into PUFcc, PUFsecurity won TSMC OIP Partner of the Year, deploying into N5/N3/N2 nodes. Patented active zeroization circuits destroy keys within microseconds of physical optical tamper detection, securing PSA Certified Level 3 and SESIP Level 3 certifications.
